2. The allegation is that on 23.03.2015, the Food Safety Officer inspected Archana Bakery,
Marangattupally, and purchased banana chips, and the samples were sent for chemical analysis.

It was tested as per standard food safety 2025:KER:69312 CRL.REV.PET NO. 338 OF 2023 parameters and found non-conforming as it shows the presence of Synthetic colour Tartrazine,
which is in contravention of the rules.
3.Thereafter, the respondents filed an application for discharge before the learned Magistrate as C.M.P No. 4101(A)/2019.
4.The learned Magistrate, as per the impugned order, invoked Section 258 Cr. P.C. and accordingly dropped the proceedings against the accused.
Aggrieved by the same, this revision petition is filed by the Food Safety Officer.
Heard Additional Director General of Prosecution and Adv. Tom Jose for the respondents.

5. Admittedly, the petitioner filed a private complaint before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Pala, alleging offences under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) regulations 2011.

sentences.text: 2 7. Section 258 Cr.P.C is extracted hereunder:-
"258. Power to stop proceedings in certain cases.

In any summons-case instituted otherwise than upon complaint, a Magistrate of the first class or, with the previous sanction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, any other Judicial Magistrate, may, for reasons to be recorded by him, stop the proceedings at any stage without pronouncing any judgment and where such stoppage of proceedings is made after the evidence of the principal witnesses has been recorded, pronounce a judgment of acquittal, and in any other case, release the accused, and such release shall have the effect of discharge."
8.A reading of Section 258 Cr.P.C, it is clear that, the section is applicable to police charge cases.
Admittedly, the present case is not a summons case instituted other than upon a complaint.
If that is the case, the dropping of proceedings invoking Section 258 Cr.P.C is illegal.
Therefore, the impugned order is to be set aside.

But I make it clear that all the contentions raised by the respondents are left open and the 2025:KER:69312 CRL.REV.PET NO. 338 OF 2023 petitioner is free to agitate the same before the trial court at the appropriate stage, but the impugned order has to be set aside, and the complaint is to be restored.

Accordingly, the revision is allowed in the following manner;
a)The order dated 30.07.2019 in C.M.P No.4104(A)/2019 in C.C No.314/2016 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Pala is set aside and C.C No.314/2016

sentences.text: is restored.

b)The Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I Pala will proceed with C.C. No.314/2016, in accordance with law.
c)All the contentions raised by the respondents are left open.
